problem:
A rectangular plate occupies the region
$D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 3}$
and has mass density function $\lambda (x,y)=xy,$ where $x$ and $y$ are measured in meters.
Given that the center of mass is at $(\frac{2}{3},2),$ find the moment of inertia about a line perpendicular to $D$ at a distance of $1\,\text{m}$ from a parallel line passing through its center of mass.
worked_solution:
For a plane lamina of mass $M$ and a line ${l}_{M}$ perpendicular to the lamina passing through its center of mass, the parallel axis theorem states that the moment of inertia of the lamina about a line $l$ parallel to ${l}_{M}$ is given by

$$
{I}_{l}={I}_{M}+{d}^{2}M,
$$

where $d$ is the distance between the lines, and ${I}_{M}$ and ${I}_{l}$ are the moments of inertia about the lines ${l}_{M}$ and $l,$ respectively.

First, we find the mass of the plate as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{3}xy\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}x\,\text{d}x{\int }_{0}^{3}y\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}{|}_{0}^{1}\cdot \frac{1}{2}{y}^{2}{|}_{0}^{3} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot \frac{9}{2} \\  & =\frac{9}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, the moment of inertia about the perpendicular line through the center of mass $(\frac{2}{3},2)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{M} & ={∬}_{D}((x-\overset{¯}{x})^{2}+(y-\overset{¯}{y})^{2})\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}({(x-\frac{2}{3})}^{2}+{(y-2)}^{2})\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{3}({(x-\frac{2}{3})}^{2}+{(y-2)}^{2})xy\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{3}x{(x-\frac{2}{3})}^{2}y+x{y}^{3}-4x{y}^{2}+4xy\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{[\frac{1}{2}x{(x-\frac{2}{3})}^{2}{y}^{2}+\frac{1}{4}x{y}^{4}-\frac{4}{3}x{y}^{3}+2x{y}^{2}]}_{y=0}^{y=3}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{9}{2}x{(x-\frac{2}{3})}^{2}+\frac{81}{4}x-36x+18x\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{9}{2}x{(x-\frac{2}{3})}^{2}+\frac{9}{4}x\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{9}{2}{x}^{3}-6{x}^{2}+\frac{17}{4}x\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{9}{8}{x}^{4}-2{x}^{3}+\frac{17}{8}{x}^{2}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{9}{8}-2+\frac{17}{8}-0 \\  & =\frac{5}{4}\,\text{kg}\cdot {\text{m}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, applying the parallel axis theorem, the moment of inertia about a line $1\,\text{m}$ from the center of mass is

$$
\begin{aligned}I & ={I}_{M}+{d}^{2}M \\  & =\frac{5}{4}+{(1)}^{2}\cdot \frac{9}{4} \\  & =\frac{5}{4}+\frac{9}{4} \\  & =\frac{7}{2}\,\text{kg}\cdot {\text{m}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
